findings.heading: Log rank test
findings.proposition: The English states the log-rank test gives enough evidence of a survival difference by source of infection at alpha = 0.005; the Japanese states alpha = 0.05.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader takes the significance threshold used in this example to be 0.05 and copies the looser level into their own interpretation, so they judge the same result against a criterion ten times weaker than the one the English text applies.

findings.heading: Data management and transformation
findings.proposition: The English says the new columns are checked with summary() on futime AND a cross-tabulation of event against outcome; the Japanese says the check is a cross-tabulation of futime, event and outcome, which the chunk at lines 143-151 does not do (it runs summary(linelist_surv$futime) and tabyl(outcome, event)).
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader looks for a cross-tabulation involving futime in the code below, does not find one, and does not learn that a continuous follow-up time is checked with summary() rather than with a table.

findings.heading: Log rank test
findings.proposition: The English CAUTION states that survminer functions in general require the data argument to be given again alongside the survival object; the Japanese restricts the requirement to ggsurvplot().
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader applies the rule only to ggsurvplot(), then hits the same non-specific error with another survminer function such as ggforest() or ggcoxzph() and does not know the cause.

findings.heading: Time-dependent covariate setup
findings.proposition: The English says the BMT dataset is loaded from the survival package; the Japanese says it is loaded from the SemiCompRisks package.
findings.reader_consequence: The two editions disagree about which package supplies BMT. The Japanese matches the chunk data(BMT, package = "SemiCompRisks"), so a reader who cross-checks against the English text, or who reads the English first, installs or searches the wrong package.

findings.heading: Time-dependent covariate setup
findings.proposition: The English states that TA is the time in days to acute graft-versus-host disease; the Japanese variable list drops the unit 'days' for TA, although it keeps it for T1.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader does not learn the time unit of TA, so they cannot read the interval boundaries in the reshaped data (for example patient 1 changing agvhd at time 67) as days.

findings.heading: Fitting a Cox model
findings.proposition: The English defines the printed p-value as the probability that the estimated coefficient could be 0; the Japanese says only that it is the p-value of the test of whether the coefficient is 0, and gives no definition.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader gets a circular gloss and no statement of what the printed p-value measures, so the bullet list of Cox output columns explains every column except that one.

findings.heading: Load packages
findings.proposition: The Japanese opens the paragraph with a sentence stating that running the code below loads the packages needed for the analysis. The English has no such sentence.
findings.reader_consequence: Minor: the Japanese reader is told the following chunk loads the packages, a claim the English leaves implicit. The Japanese chunk at line 49 also drops echo=F, so the chunk is shown, which makes the added sentence consistent with the Japanese page but not with the English one.
